The per-layer scan puts L11 in a class of its own. Its end-of-prompt value is 7.4 times its answer-token value and almost purely math-conditional (math 16.0, poem 1.1, conditioning 0.93). Other layers show one property or the other, but not both:
- L18 has a similar ratio (7.3) but no math-conditioning (−0.07; the poem is higher).
- L20 and L13 are as math-conditional (0.93, 0.88) but have ordinary ratios (2.3, 2.7).
- Math-conditioning builds up smoothly from L6 to L13 (0.24 → 0.88), so it is a natural task representation.

L10 is the only partial match: ratio 4.68 (third), conditioning 0.72, and the second-highest value-projection gain on the math direction (1.13). It is the one credible place for a weaker second broadcast channel.

I test it directly rather than argue from statistics. The candidate is V1 plus the identical recipe at L10: remove from L10's `v_proj` the unit direction of its mean end-of-prompt value. Before the pass, I check on summary vectors what this does: L10's component before and after, its overlap with the math-minus-poem value difference, and how much of the mean answer-token value lies along it. I also check how exactly the original model's answers reproduce between passes 27 and 32 on DEV[0:256]. If they reproduce well, comparing V1+L10 with V1's answers on the same problems is close to a paired comparison.

Prediction: if L10 is an accomplice, V1+L10 will beat V1's +25.4 on this slice with extra wrong→right flips. If L10 is just natural task encoding, the gain will be equal or lower, and I close this line.

The original model's answers reproduced exactly between passes 27 and 32: every text is identical. Comparing a new edit's answers with V1's answers from pass 27 on the same 256 problems is therefore effectively a paired comparison.

The L10 candidate is saved together with V1:
- L10's end-of-prompt value component falls from 1.136 to 0.002, a 6.3% relative change to that tensor.
- The removed direction is only moderately aligned with L10's math-minus-poem value difference (cos 0.76, against 0.94 at L11).
- It also carries about 20% of the mean answer-token value, so it is less purely a prompt-end channel than L11's.

That makes a natural, useful component somewhat more likely than a plant, but only the pass can decide. I now run V1+L10 paired on DEV[0:256].
- If it beats V1's 47.7% accuracy with net extra wrong→right flips relative to V1, L10 is a second channel worth confirming.
- If it is equal or lower, I close the L10 line.

V1+L10 gives **+25.4 ± 3.2** on DEV[0:256] (74 wrong→right, 9 right→wrong), with accuracy 47.66%. That is exactly V1's accuracy on the same problems. Removing L10's end-of-prompt value direction adds nothing, so L10 is natural task encoding and not a second plant. I close that line and restore V1 alone.

To see how much the extra L10 change merely reshuffles answers, I count the problems that V1+L10 and V1 (pass 27) get right individually, using the exact reproducibility shown above.

Next I look again at head 3 of L11, the head that wrote the oversized broadcast. My notes say its output matrix is 1.3–1.7× its siblings across the spectrum, and that per-head output norms range 0.69–1.63× across the model. If L11 head 3 is that model-wide maximum, its oversize may be part of the plant, amplifying the broadcast. Then shrinking h3 back to its siblings' norm on top of V1 would be a principled test. If it ranks among many similar heads, its size is natural and I leave it alone.

V1+L10 and V1 differ on 64 of the 256 problems: 32 right only under V1, 32 right only under V1+L10, with only 2% of texts identical. The L10 change shuffles answers without any net effect. This also calibrates my tests. Two similar edits churn about a quarter of the answers, so a 256-problem pass can resolve only large differences (about 6–8 points or more), not small tweaks.

L11 head 3 does have the model's largest output-projection norm relative to its layer (1.44×). But the top of that distribution is smooth (L25h0 1.42, L14h0 1.37, L4h3 1.35), so head 3's size is not a separate planted anomaly. My earlier dose scan showed it has a useful function (zeroing it was worse than scaling it to 0.2), so I will not shrink it on top of V1.
